card.name: Object words in formal policy prose
card.fires_on: The last word of a verb phrase in formal government or policy-style text, often a noun or pronoun object such as progress, contribution, change, or it. A clause or sentence often ends or turns right after it.

modes.label: Policy object nouns
modes.description: A noun that completes a verb in government policy text, such as monitor progress or promote change.
modes.example: The Commission's main responsibility will be to monitor<< progress>> on sustainable development, and to build consensus

modes.label: Pronoun or verb ending a clause
modes.description: A pronoun like it or a word like needed or returning that closes a clause in formal prose.
modes.example: so that<< it>> is targeted at the problem in hand;

card.writes: It leans toward words like proper, properly and Afterwards, and away from Whilst and firstly.
card.plain: It fires on the word that completes a phrase in formal policy writing, such as the object of a verb.
